FIRST-REQUEST BYTE IDENTITY, stated honestly before contact. The first request of a row is the Perception request, and under this factor it is NOT byte-identical to the base's: the system message carries the constant L0+L1 index as a suffix of the contract fill, and the row's pointer block plus budgeted expansions replace the per-row slot-contract cards and the raw exemplar block. What IS claimed, and what the smoke proves, is (a) ONE system-message sha256 over every contact of every row (the index is constant), (b) no byte before the expansion block moves relative to the render proof's prediction, (c) the index receipt (view id, release and snapshot pins, per-contact selected ids) is present on every contact, and (d) no request carries a tools array. A second system-message sha, a missing receipt or a tools array is a FAILURE. A differing Solver, Reviewer or Planner request whose upstream model response differs is reported, not silently excused: greedy decoding at temperature 0 is not bitwise reproducible across batch compositions. For the twin, additionally: the rendered header keeps the SOURCE view id (so no byte before the index body shifts), and the per-row expansion block is NOT byte-matched to IDX's at slot_card 4 (the deranged L2 cards differ in length per row; mean absolute difference about 641 characters, sum zero over the 54 cards) -- the per-row length-difference distribution is a mandatory table of the twin read.

COST: actual generation contacts against the anchor's realized 5,417 and the 11,880 ceiling; actual repeated speech seconds against the anchor's realized 15,459.76; actual FIT endpoints; GPU hours read from the serving monitor over the lease window.

INDEX CONSUMPTION (owner emphasis 2026-09-20, decision 61). An index that looks reasonable may be unconsumable by the frozen core because an L0/L1 line carries too little reference information; this read decides that question with the sealed outputs and receipts alone, model-free. (a) CITATIONS: Solver outputs that cite index ids -- count, distinct ids, resolved versus unresolved, share of rows with at least one citation, and whether a cited id's line or card is consistent with the delivered intent / slot types. (b) POINTER USE: per row, whether the delivered intent lies in the row's pointer-block intent set and whether the delivered slot types lie in the pointed slot set; the same shares computed on the BASE's sealed outputs against the SAME pointer blocks (rendered model-free from the sealed receipts), so that 'the answer follows the pointers' is measured against 'the answer would have followed them anyway'. (c) EXPANSION USE: for slot types whose L2 card was expanded on a row versus slot types only pointed, the delivered slot-type precision / recall and the filler format-compliance rate against the L1 'Admissible formats' line (one regex per slot type derived from the view), on this cell and on the base. (d) FORMAT COMPLIANCE overall: the share of delivered fillers matching an admissible format, this cell versus the base versus the other index cell. (e) THE TRIPLE: base / IDX / IDXT on official SLU-F1 and intent. CONSUMPTION is evidenced when IDX differs from IDXT beyond the own null AND (a)-(d) move in the same direction as the score; NON-CONSUMPTION is evidenced when IDX lies inside IDXT's null, citations are near zero and (b)-(d) do not move against the base; MISLEADING TERSENESS is evidenced when IDX lies below the base with (d) worse. Each of the three is stated in the verdict with its evidence, or 'undecided' with the reason. CONTINGENCY, fixed here: on NON-CONSUMPTION the next cell is the richer-granularity variant of the same view on the same base (intent L2 activation cards through expansion_budget.intent_card > 0 and / or a larger slot_card budget; a new one-factor registration), not the closure of the index form; on MISLEADING TERSENESS the form is closed at decision 52's defaults and the owner decides; on CONSUMPTION the decision rule's own verdict stands. For the twin, (b)-(d) are computed against the twin's own deranged pointer blocks and cards: they are the null reference of pointer use and expansion use, and a twin whose pointer-use share equals IDX's is direct evidence that the pointers were not read.

resume_recovery_clause: owner decision 22 of 2026-09-18. If an attempt dies of an INFRASTRUCTURE failure with code and request bytes unchanged -- never a harness or config defect -- the one allowed recovery may be a RESUME-RECOVERY under item E10 instead of a re-fly: every complete row of the aborted attempt is kept without selection, every partial or unstarted row is flown under the same run id, and the merged manifest declares the predecessor attempt with its trace hash, kept-row list and that list's hash. It changes no question, roster, factor, comparator, decision rule or cap, and the run-cumulative budget must be re-checked because a resumed attempt and its predecessor share one run id. A resumed EFFICIENCY read must additionally state the split of its GPU hours and prefilled tokens across attempts, because a merged manifest's cost is the sum of two lease windows and a per-row rate computed over the merged manifest alone would be wrong.
